Definition: from G4253 and G71; to lead forward (magisterially); intransitively, to precede (in place or time [particle previous]):--bring (forth, out), go before.
BiblicalUsage: Proago means to go before, to lead forward, to precede. Paul charges Timothy by the prophecies which went before on him, and John warns that whoever goes onward and abides not in the doctrine of Christ has not God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe going before is the leader's job, and the test of any leader is whether he stays in the doctrine of Christ.
